title: WhatsApp rolling out redesigned iPad interface with Mac-like sidebar
snippet: Following a few months of Liquid Glass beta testing, WhatsApp is expanding access to a redesigned interface for its iPad app, including a new Mac-like sidebar. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Following a few months of Liquid Glass beta testing, WhatsApp is expanding access to a redesigned interface for its iPad app, including a new Mac-like sidebar. Here are the details.

WhatsApp working on new iPad app layout

Although WhatsApp initially started working on adapting its iOS app for the Liquid Glass visual overhaul last October, the company only brought the redesign to iPad much later, with a limited beta test last June.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the redesign included Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons, and context menus, while retaining the same bottom tab bar used on iPhone.

Image: WABetaInfo

Now, the site reports that WhatsApp is rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, with a new Mac-like sidebar replacing the bottom tab bar by default.

The sidebar, which mirrors the layout already available on WhatsApp for Mac, provides quick access to Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls, Meta AI, and other sections of the app. Users can also hide it to give more space to the chat list and conversation view.

Image: WABetaInfo

From the report:

The sidebar takes up a portion of the screen. On iPad, this is rarely a problem since the display is large enough to show the sidebar, the chat list, and the conversation interface. However, some users may prefer a larger conversation interface. When users hide the sidebar, WhatsApp expands the chat list and the conversation toward the center of the screen, making both feel less compressed. Users who prefer to keep focus on the conversation will notice the difference immediately.

WABetaInfo notes that the new sidebar is available to some beta testers running the latest TestFlight build, although some users on the regular App Store version are also beginning to see it.

As is often the case with WhatsApp rollouts, it may take some time before the new interface reaches everyone, whether they’re using the beta or stable version of the app. Still, iPad users should benefit from the more tablet-friendly layout once it becomes available to them.

title: Is the iPhone Duo just the start, with most iPhones foldable within a decade?
snippet: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has made an interesting prediction in his latest newsletter, suggesting that the iPhone Duo is just the start and that most iPhones will be foldable within a decade. He argues that in that kind of timescale, even budget devices like the iPhone SE could go foldable as manufacturing costs fall … more…
fullText:
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has made an interesting prediction in his latest newsletter, suggesting that the iPhone Duo is just the start and that most iPhones will be foldable within a decade.

He argues that in that kind of timescale, even budget devices like the iPhone SE could go foldable as manufacturing costs fall … 

Prior to the launch of the iPhone Duo, foldables are an incredibly niche product, accounting for just 2% of the global smartphone market. Despite its high price tag, the Duo is expected to change this significantly over the course of the next 12 months.

Counterpoint Research predicted last week that the foldable market will grow 24% in the remainder of this year and a further 37% next year. The firm also predicts that Apple will take a 40% market share within that timescale, which could make it the leading player in the market.

In his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman looks further ahead.

My prediction is that, within a decade, foldables will make up the majority of new phone sales. Users will increasingly see the benefits of having a larger display in their pocket and a device that can replace a laptop or tablet for many tasks. Foldables could become the do-it-all computing products of the future.

	

He suggests that Apple could go both up and down the price ladder with future foldables. He sees an iPhone Duo Max with a larger display and bigger price tag as one possibility, but also an iPhone SE in the company’s future.

9to5Mac’s Take

A decade is an extremely long time in tech, so almost anything could happen within that kind of timescale – if, indeed, humanity survives that long. It’s certainly well within the bounds of possibility that the foldable format could become ubiquitous thanks to falling manufacturing costs.

A likely next step is to find a way to embed Face ID into the device. This is technically easier than the selfie camera sitting beneath the interior display, so the challenge here is to manage the depth of the Face ID array on the outer screen without making the device any thicker.

What do you think of Gurman’s prediction? Please take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments.

title: The EOS R8 Mark II is Canon’s lightest full-frame camera with stabilization
snippet: Canon announced the second-generation of its EOS R8 with a new retro-inspired redesign and the addition of in-body stabilization. The Canon EOS R8 Mark II is expected to be available sometime in late October for $1,899 for … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Canon announced the second-generation of its EOS R8 with a new retro-inspired redesign and the addition of in-body stabilization. That feature was one of the most notable omissions from the original R8 that launched in 2023 as a smaller, cheaper, and more accessible alternative to the Canon R6 Mark II for photographers wanting a larger full-frame shooter. While the new EOS R8 Mark II is slightly heavier than its predecessor at 1.2 pounds thanks to the additional stabilization functionality, it’s lighter and cheaper than last year’s EOS R6 Mark III.

The Canon EOS R8 Mark II is expected to be available sometime in late October for $1,899 for the body only, or $2,099 bundled with a Canon 24-50mm stabilized lens. That’s more expensive than the original R8 that launched at $1,499, but more accessible than the $2,799 EOS R6 Mark III thanks to some lower specs and omitted features.

Like its predecessor, the R8 Mark II features the same 24.2-megapixel full-frame CMOS sensor as the R6 Mark II, while the R6 Mark III got a bump to a 32.5-megapixel sensor. The new R8 Mark II still exclusively uses an electronic shutter instead of an additional mechanical one, with high-speed captures maxing out at 40fps again. To ensure you’re not too late to a critical moment, a pre-continuous shooting mode captures up to an additional 20 shots before you press the shutter button.

Image: Canon

The new five-axis in-body stabilization offers up to 7.5 stops of shake correction that can be expanded by pairing the camera with a lens featuring its own stabilization. The R8 Mark II also features Canon’s Dual Pixel CMOS AF II system with what the company describes as “more tenacious tracking” than what the R8 offered. The autofocus system can also recognize animals, vehicles, and people, with the option to register up to 10 different people by their faces and rank their priority.

Video capabilities max out at 4K/60fps, but frame rates can be boosted to up to 180fps by dropping the resolution to 1080p. As Canon is targeting the R8 Mark II as a potential full-frame option for amateur photographers, the camera includes 16 different color filters, an easy to way to increase or decrease depth of blur that handles settings like f-stop and shutter speed automatically, and creative bracketing that takes three photos with different brightness and color tones.

Image: Canon

Following other companies drawing inspiration from older film cameras for the design of new digital shooters, the R8 Mark II eschews the curves of the original R8 for a more boxy and angular body. Canon credits the nearly 40-year-old EOS 650 and its pentaprism housing on top as the inspiration for the R8 Mark II. Other hardware upgrades include a new multi-controller joystick above the camera’s screen, which makes it easier to select focal points, and its single SD card slot repositioned on the side of the camera so it’s still accessible when using a tripod. Canon will also sell a matching $99.99 accessory that extends the R8 Mark II’s grip, making it easier to hold when using larger lenses.

In October Canon is also releasing a free new Windows app called Dual Pixel 3D Converter that leverages additional info captured by Canon’s dual-pixel autofocus system to generate 3D imagery from the 2D photos the camera takes. You can use the app to create a 3D photo with a background you can move around, a 3D model with the background completely removed, or short 3D videos demonstrating an animated perspective adjustment of close-up subjects.

Given Samsung’s poor track record on the robustness and reliability of its foldable phones, it’s not surprising that it felt threatened by the build quality of the iPhone Duo. Even before the new model was officially unveiled, the company was criticizing the reported weight of the device.

Once it was announced, it was clear that Apple had addressed a key weakness of Samsung’s foldables: vulnerability to damage caused by the ingress of dust and dirt. While Samsung’s latest folding model is only rated to IP48, leaving it vulnerable to particles as large as a grain of sand, the iPhone Duo is rated to IP68, meaning fully dustproof.

Samsung now appears to be hoping that if one fold isn’t enough, perhaps two will do the trick. Our sister site 9to5Google spotted a report suggesting Samsung plans to bring forward the launch of the Galaxy Z Trifold 2 in direct response to the iPhone Duo.

This would be a more surprising move given that the original dual-fold model wasn’t exactly a market or financial success.

The original TriFold made its US debut in January for $2,900 and was discontinued barely three months later [amid] rumors that it was sold at a loss.

Next year’s model is expected to sell for roughly the same price as the original.

title: PS Plus Gets a Diverse Lineup for September With WWE 2K26, RuneScape: Dragonwilds and More
snippet: From the supernatural horror of Slitterhead to the roguelite action of Ball x Pit and the stealthy combat of Sniper Elite: Resistance, this month’s additions offer plenty of ways to play.
fullText:
It’s September 2026, and the avalanche of quality games is already underway with Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Star Wars Zero Company and Marvel’s Wolverine. The big game releases will continue to happen weekly until Nov. 19, when Grand Theft Auto 6 releases, but this month, PS Plus subscribers are getting a mix of action, fantasy and a sprinkle of quirky games added to the service.

PS Plus, which is Sony’s version of Xbox Game Pass, offers a large, constantly expanding library of games. Subscribers can choose from the Essential, Extra and Premium tiers, each with unique perks and benefits. Starting at $11 per month, the plans give subscribers access to games and rewards, and each month, subscribers can play a handful of new games at no additional charge. 

If you’re a PlayStation Plus Extra or Premium subscriber, you can grab these games now.

Set on the forgotten continent of Ashenfall, RuneScape: Dragonwilds is a cooperative survival RPG where players must gather resources, craft gear, build shelters and develop their skills to survive a land filled with dangerous creatures. The adventure combines classic RuneScape lore with survival mechanics and a new fantasy setting. Players can unlock abilities and spells as they progress, while quests lead them through a hand-crafted world filled with familiar enemies and new threats. At the center of the adventure is a confrontation with the fearsome Dragon Queen.

RuneScape: Dragonwilds is available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers on Tuesday.

WWE 2K26 

WWE 2K26 puts hundreds of WWE Superstars and legends at your fingertips, combining wrestling simulation with a variety of ways to play out your own version of WWE history. The massive roster includes modern stars alongside icons from the Attitude Era, while Showcase mode focuses on CM Punk and explores alternate versions of his career. Players can also rewrite wrestling history through fantasy scenarios, allowing them to revisit famous rivalries and imagine how things might have unfolded differently. It’s a wrestling game built around both authenticity and fan-driven fantasy.

WWE 2K26 is available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers on Tuesday.

Ball x Pit

A ruined city, a bottomless pit and an army of monsters set the stage for Ball x Pit, a fast-paced fantasy roguelite built around frantic combat and progression. Players descend through increasingly difficult levels while using magic-infused projectiles to battle enemies and overcome obstacles. Between runs, they can develop new ammunition and resources, recruit additional heroes and work toward rebuilding the destroyed city of New Ballbylon. Its combination of arcade-style action, randomized challenges and character progression gives each attempt a different feel as players push deeper into the pit.

Ball x Pit will be available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers starting Sept. 22.

Date Everything!

When a woman loses her customer service job to AI, a mysterious gift gives her a bizarre new career path: dating the objects in her own house. Date Everything! turns the traditional dating simulator into a comedic adventure where magical Dateviator glasses bring everyday items to life. Each object has its own personality, story and relationship path, and your choices can lead to friendship, romance or conflict. The game blends visual novel storytelling, relationship management and comedy, with a huge cast of voiced characters hidden among the furniture and appliances around your home.

Date Everything! is already available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers.

Slitterhead

Set in the neon-soaked streets of Kowloon, Slitterhead is a horror action-adventure that follows Hyoki, a mysterious entity without a physical body or memories. His goal is to hunt Slitterheads, monstrous creatures that disguise themselves as humans. Combat revolves around manipulating blood and working alongside special humans known as Rarities, who can help Hyoki infiltrate dangerous groups and take down enemies. As the investigation unfolds, players uncover the mystery surrounding Hyoki and the creatures haunting the city. The result is a dark blend of supernatural horror, action and investigative storytelling.

Slitterhead will be available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers starting Sept. 22.

Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound

Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound brings the classic series into a modern 2D action-platformer, combining the fast combat and lore of the original games with ideas inspired by the newer 3D entries. When the barrier between the human and demon worlds breaks, Hayabusa Village is overrun while Ryu Hayabusa is away. Young ninja Kenji Mozu must step up and defend his home from the invading forces. Developed by the team behind Blasphemous, Ragebound emphasizes precise movement, aggressive combat and challenging enemies in a stylish side-scrolling adventure.

Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound will be available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers starting Sept. 29.

Dungeons of Hinterberg

Corporate burnout takes Luisa to the Austrian Alps, where a quiet vacation town hides a network of mysterious dungeons. Dungeons of Hinterberg mixes action-adventure gameplay with puzzle solving, exploration and social simulation. Players can snowboard across snowy landscapes, climb mountains, explore the countryside, and tackle dungeons filled with magical abilities and unusual challenges. Time spent in town is just as important, allowing Luisa to build friendships with locals and fellow adventurers. The result is a colorful fantasy adventure that balances combat and exploration with brain-teasing puzzles and character-driven downtime.

Dungeons of Hinterberg will be available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers starting Sept. 29.

Sniper Elite: Resistance

Set behind enemy lines in occupied France, Sniper Elite: Resistance follows SOE agent Harry Hawker as he works with the French Resistance to stop a devastating Nazi superweapon. The third-person shooter emphasizes stealth, tactical combat and the series’ signature long-range sniping, giving players considerable freedom in how they approach missions. Multiple targets and different infiltration and extraction points encourage experimentation rather than a single path through each level. The campaign can also be played cooperatively, adding another layer to its mix of methodical shooting, reconnaissance and tactical action.

Sniper Elite: Resistance will be available for PS Plus Extra and Premium subscribers starting Sept. 29.

Mega Man X Command Mission

Mega Man X Command Mission puts the robot hero and his allies in the middle of a dangerous conflict over Giga City. Unlike the series’ traditional run-and-gun platformers, this adventure is a turn-based RPG, allowing players to assemble a team and combine their abilities during battles. X is joined by familiar characters, including Zero and Axl, along with new allies, as they tackle more than 50 missions. Side quests, powerful bosses and team-based combat add depth to the futuristic story, making it a notable genre shift for the Mega Man X series.

Mega Man X Command Mission is currently available for PS Plus Premium subscribers.

Metro Redux

Metro Redux combines two atmospheric first-person shooters set in a post-apocalyptic Russia where survivors live in underground stations after a devastating nuclear war. Players take control of Artyom, who ventures through the Metro tunnels and eventually into the poisoned world above while confronting mutants, hostile survivors and a growing threat to humanity. The games emphasize tense exploration, resource management, stealth and gunplay, with limited supplies making every encounter dangerous. Blending survival horror with immersive storytelling and first-person action, Metro Redux creates a bleak underground world where survival is never guaranteed.

title: Samsung Is Fast-Tracking Galaxy Z TriFold 2 After iPhone Duo Reveal, According to Leaks
snippet: The successor to Samsung’s first TriFold phone may now have an accelerated release timeline.
fullText:
Foldable phones have never exactly been a powerhouse segment of the handset market, despite being flashy pieces of technology – but when Apple enters the fray, public interest is sure to follow.

Now that the iPhone Duo has been revealed, and following strong early sales for the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra, Samsung is looking to fast-track a competing device, according to known leaker Lanzuk.

A successor to the Galaxy Z TriFold has reportedly been under development for months, with detailed patents painting a picture of what we might expect from the new phone – it could be wider and shorter and might include a slot for the S Pen stylus.

But Samsung is now reportedly considering an accelerated release timeline, which could mean the next Galaxy Z TriFold will launch in late 2026 or early 2027. Previous reports indicated that the phone would likely be slated for a late 2027 release.

	

			

The first Galaxy Z TriFold had an expensive, limited release in the US. The phone was available starting in January, and despite a commanding starting price of $2,900, it sold out quickly before being discontinued three months later. It felt like a more experimental product in Samsung’s mobile lineup, but a second TriFold might signal a more serious commitment to this design.

According to Lanzuk, Samsung wants to produce the new TriFold handset at a “nearly identical” price, despite rising hardware costs. If people are willing to turn out in droves for the high-end iPhone Duo configurations – some of which cost more than $3,000 – this could prove to be a more competitive market niche than ever before.

A Samsung representative didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

It’s worth noting that the iPhone Duo hasn’t officially hit the market yet and won’t do so for another month. All the online buzz in the world isn’t worth anything if the new foldable phone doesn’t sell well, so Samsung may be watching how the market reacts to the Duo before reallocating any development resources.

The Galaxy Z TriFold 2 has reportedly been under development for some time, so a shift in plans may signal renewed urgency and confidence in the market segment.

The iPhone Duo will be released on Oct. 23 with a starting price of $1,999.

title: MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro goes official with 2nm process and performance gains
snippet: MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process. more…
fullText:
MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process.

The Dimensity 9600 Pro has a 2+3+3 All Big Core CPU design using Arm’s new C2-Ultra cores at 4.55GHz, three C2-Pro cores at 4.35GHz, and three more C2-Pro cores at 3.1GHz. Altogether, MediaTek says that its latest design delivers 17% better single-core performance and 15% higher multi-core performance compared to last year’s chip. 

Leading where others follow, the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 is a first-wave 2nm smartphone chip design that’s built to simultaneously raise the bar on performance, capability, and power-efficiency…

At its heart is MediaTek’s 4th-generation All Big Core CPU: a revolutionary 2+3+3 design pairing two Arm C2-Ultra processors, three Arm C2-Pro processors with 1MB L2 cache and three Arm C2-Pro with 512KB L2 cache, which altogether contribute to a 21% larger L2 cache system.

…MediaTek leads the industry with first-wave support for both UFS 5.0, which delivers 2x faster read/writes than the previous generation, and LPDDR6, which boosts effective memory bandwidth by 33% at the same frequency.

This latest chip adopts LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5.0 storage. The G2-Ultra NX GPU brings a 27% boost to peak performance while hitting 24% lower power consumption. Ray-tracing is 18% faster and games support up to 185fps. 

On the AI side, Dimensity 9600 Pro’s second-gen Super Efficient NPU reduces power consumption by 40% while delivering better performance and higher token generation per watt. 

	

Rounding things out, the Imagiq 1290 ISP supports 4K240 native direct-output ultra-slow-motion video, 4K120 cinematic log, and AI-powered True Color Tone and 60fps motion capture features. 

One of the first devices powered by the Dimensity 9600 Pro will be Oppo’s Find X10 Pro Max, due to be announced next week. Meanwhile, MediaTek is also announcing the Dimensity 9600M as a lower-cost version of this chip with “flagship-level performance.” It lacks UFS 5.0 and uses Arm’s C1 cores instead of C2.

title: Google’s New Pixel Features Include Shortcuts to Your Favorite Contacts, Adds Scam Alerts
snippet: The September Pixel Drop includes two months of Audible for anyone with a Pixel 6 or newer.
fullText:
Google is giving Pixel users faster ways to reach frequent contacts, a new scam alert to fend off fraudulent texts and two months of Audible access coinciding with the launch of new Harry Potter audiobooks.

The September feature drop comes a month after the release of Google’s Pixel 11 line, and these features will be available to anyone using the Pixel 6 or newer.

	

			

An update to Google’s Pixel VIP feature — which lets you designate up to eight contacts as close friends and family — lets you create home screen widgets that can tap to easily call or text your favorite people. If you call someone especially frequently, you won’t need to dig through your phone or text app first.

Google’s new Scam Detection alerts in the Gboard keyboard will work across chat apps, showing a warning pop-up when the phone detects a likely scam text message. This feature joins the existing Scam Detection alerts in notifications, which are getting a regional expansion with support for more languages.

Scam Detection alerts are coming to the Gboard keyboard on Pixel phones.Google

Pixel phones will receive Harry Potter theme packs for customizing your device’s home screen, icons and sounds, which are coming as part of a promotional tie-in with the Audible release of Harry Potter: The Full-Cast Audio Editions audiobook. Anyone with a Pixel 6 or newer will get the packs, along with an offer for two months of Audible access, whether or not you want to stream Harry Potter.

Google’s also updating its Pixel Watch this week, with improvements to how its raise-to-talk gesture works on the Pixel Watch 4 and 5, along with adding a one-handed pinch gesture for opening your notification tray on the Pixel Watch 3 and newer.

Google’s Pixel Drop comes as Apple just released iOS 27, which adds the updated Siri AI along with an assortment of AI features, to the iPhone 15 Pro and newer. Apple’s iOS 27 works on devices as old as 2019’s iPhone 11, promising performance improvements along with an overhauled device search.

title: Which new Apple products will launch this year – and which won’t?
snippet: Apple may still be cleaning up after the end of the iPhone launch, but attention is already turning to an October event. There are still a lot of new products we’re expecting the company to unveil, with the most exciting of these including touchscreen MacBooks and a smart home hub we’ve been dubbing the HomePad. But which ones will launch this year, and which ones will have to wait until next year … ? more…
fullText:
Apple may still be cleaning up after the end of the iPhone launch, but attention is already turning to an October event.

There are still a lot of new products we’re expecting the company to unveil, with the most exciting of these including touchscreen MacBooks and a smart home hub we’ve been dubbing the HomePad. But which ones will launch this year, and which ones will have to wait until next year … ?

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has laid out his latest expectations. He’s still being a little coy with exact timings, simply saying that some products will launch “later this year” rather than specifically in an October event. That could potentially allow for some launches next month and others closer to the end of the year.

This year

Gurman says we can expect six new products later this year:

Touchscreen MacBook Pro models (likely in 14- and 16-inch versions)

An updated 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip (non-touchscreen model)

A new iMac, although this will only be new colors and an M6 processor

HomePod mini 2, with Siri AI

Apple TV 4K, with Siri AI

iPad mini, with OLED screen

However, he still has no answer on whether we can expect to see the launch of the HomePad, stating that while it may launch in October, the timeline is “likely still fluid.”

First half of 2027

The iPhone Air 2 is potentially the most significant of the product launches expected in the first half of next year. This is expected to add an ultrawide camera and to offer improved battery life. The iPad Air is also expected to get an OLED screen for the first time, as well as a more powerful chip.

The rest of the list is lengthy, but mostly comprises iterative updates:

IPhone 18, mostly expected to be the iPhone 17 with A20 chip

IPhone 18e, likewise only seeing a chip upgrade

MacBook Air models with M6 chip

MacBook Neo with an A19 Pro chip

Entry-level iPad with Siri AI support

iPad Pro models with chip and cooling upgrades

Two Apple Pencil updates, both expected to be compatible with the iPhone Duo

Later in 2027

Things are, however, expected to get much more interesting in the second half of next year. 

Smart glasses; AirPods with built-in cameras; a home security system and related device; a redesigned Apple Watch; a 20th-anniversary iPhone line; and a second-generation iPhone Duo.

title: Apple files Supreme Court brief challenging contempt ruling in Epic case [U]
snippet: Apple today formalized its challenge to the contempt ruling in its long-running legal battle with Epic Games, filing its opening merits brief with the U.S. Supreme Court. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today formalized its challenge to the contempt ruling in its long-running legal battle with Epic Games, filing its opening merits brief with the U.S. Supreme Court. Here are the details.

A bit of context

As 9to5Mac readers know, the Supreme Court recently accepted Apple’s request to review a contempt ruling in the lawsuit Epic Games brought against the company in 2020.

In a nutshell, although Apple came out on top on most of Epic Games’ claims in the original lawsuit, it lost on one key point, with the court finding that Apple’s anti-steering rules violated California’s Unfair Competition Law.

As a result, the court issued a permanent injunction requiring Apple to allow developers to include links and other calls to action that direct users to third-party payment options.

The order read:

Apple Inc. and its officers, agents, servants, employees, and any person in active concert or participation with them (“Apple”), are hereby permanently restrained and enjoined from prohibiting developers from (i) including in their apps and their metadata buttons, external links, or other calls to action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms, in addition to In-App Purchasing and (ii) communicating with customers through points of contact obtained voluntarily from customers through account registration within the app.

Apple changed its rules to allow those links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. When Epic challenged the company’s compliance plan, the court agreed with the Fortnite maker and held Apple in contempt for violating the injunction.

Today’s brief

In today’s brief, Apple notes that when it “filed its notice of compliance on January 16, 2024, the district court did not raise any immediate concern.”

Apple adds that Epic itself acknowledged that the injunction “did not explicitly prohibit” the company from charging a commission on purchases made outside the App Store. Still, Epic argued that the new commission and related rules violated the “spirit” of the injunction, and the district court agreed.

Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn the contempt finding, arguing that there was nothing in the original injunction that prohibited it from charging a commission. This is the ruling Apple is now asking the Supreme Court to reverse.

Today, Apple filed its official opening merits brief, laying out its case for why the contempt ruling should be overturned.

Apple argues that “civil contempt for violation of an order may not be imposed unless an order provides clear notice that the conduct at issue is proscribed,” and cites past court decisions to support its case that “a party may not be held in contempt unless an order leaves no fair ground of doubt that it prohibits the particular conduct at issue.”

From the filing:

When it comes to “contempt proceedings,” therefore, an order’s “terms” govern. Terminal R.R. Ass’n of St. Louis v. United States, 266 U.S. 17, 29 (1924). Only “a plain violation of the decree so read” can justify contempt. Id. And an alleged contemnor’s intent is irrelevant: ‘Since the purpose [of civil contempt] is remedial, it matters not with what intent the defendant did the prohibited act. McComb v. Jacksonville Paper Co., 336 U.S. 187, 191 (1949); see Taggart, 587 U.S. at 561. What matters is that the order giving rise to contempt afford clear notice to the parties. Needless to say, silence is not enough. See, e.g., Perez v. Danbury Hosp., 347 F.3d 419, 425 (2d Cir. 2003) (vacating contempt order resting on conduct as to which the court order was “silent”).

Apple also takes aim at the Ninth Circuit’s broader standard, arguing that it is an outlier in allowing parties to be held in contempt for violating the “spirit” of an injunction. According to Apple, that approach lets courts decide after the fact that conduct was prohibited even when the injunction itself never clearly said so.

Apple also argues that allowing the contempt finding to stand would increase the risk of judicial overreach when courts enforce injunctions:

That approach not only fails to afford parties the explicit notice this Court’s precedents require, but it also amplifies the unique risk of abuse threatened by the contempt power. Courts have the power to modify or clarify injunctions on a going-forward basis to address new or changed circumstances, but the severe remedy of contempt is limited to situations in which a party violates the unambiguous terms of an order.

With Apple’s opening merits brief now filed, Epic has until November 13 to file its response, with Apple’s reply due December 14. The case could then be heard by the Supreme Court as early as January 2027.

title: New Streaming Service Alert: JustWatch Is Starting Its Own Platform
snippet: You’ll be able to watch an assortment of TV shows and movies from select distributors and production houses.
fullText:
JustWatch, the streaming guide that tells you where to watch movies, TV shows or sports events, is launching a new streaming service. The company shared the news during an appearance at the Toronto International Film Festival on Tuesday, where Quentin Carbonell, JustWatch’s senior VP of global content and strategy, said JustWatch TV will be available in October. 

Viewers will have access to three options on the platform, including a free ad-based streaming service, titles available to rent or purchase, and a paid subscription offering. Upon launch, JustWatch TV’s catalog will carry content from several providers, including Fremantle, Paramount and Bleecker Street, and you’ll be able to watch within the app.

What’s a little extra about the service is that if a title isn’t available on the JustWatch TV streaming platform, the app will point you to where you can stream it, even if it’s on another platform like Hulu or Netflix. Because it’s built into the existing JustWatch website and app, functionality from the company’s ubiquitous streaming guide will be part of the streaming service itself. 

JustWatch TV will first roll out in the US, along with France, Germany, Canada, the UK, Ireland, Austria, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Australia and New Zealand. The company plans to expand its library and regional availability in the future. 

Pricing for the paid version has not been revealed, but it’s set to offer movies only with no ad breaks. The free, ad-supported option will have TV shows and movies available. 

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Kourtnee Jackson
						

						

							Senior Editor						
					

											

								

											Kourtnee covers streaming services and entertainment. She previously worked as an entertainment reporter at Endgame 360, where she wrote about film, television, music, celebrities and streaming platforms.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate now available, here is everything new
snippet: After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to everyone, bringing Apple’s new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major Safari additions, and a long list of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here’s everything new. more…
fullText:
After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to everyone, bringing Apple’s new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major Safari additions, and a long list of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here’s everything new.

During this year’s WWDC, Apple presented its operating systems somewhat differently than users and developers were used to.

Rather than introducing new features for each platform individually, Apple spent relatively little time on each operating system and focused much of the event on cross-platform features and improvements, largely because many of them rely on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

That said, macOS 27 Golden Gate still includes several welcome improvements of its own, both in design and functionality, starting with some much-needed tweaks to Liquid Glass.

Liquid Glass and UI improvements

While macOS Tahoe 26 featured Apple’s revamped look, it fell short visually compared to other systems, particularly iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple spent some time further integrating the new Liquid Glass into the system, while also bringing over some of the visual tweaks introduced in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. That includes a new Liquid Glass slider, which lets users customize just how transparent or opaque they want the effect to be.

The Liquid Glass appearance setting also includes a fun little easter egg featuring Clarus the Dogcow, which appears when you scroll the demo pane all the way down, and then keep going.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also introduces revamped app icons, more in tune with the Liquid Glass look, with additional layers that add depth and detail across light, dark, tinted, and all-clear global system settings.

The same goes for the revamped traffic light buttons Apple introduced midway through the beta period. Rather than the old flat green, yellow, and red controls, they now feature a Liquid Glass look, complete with a playful bouncing effect when users click (or perhaps, soon, touch?) and drag them before letting go.

Another welcome interface improvement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple’s decision to standardize the corner radius across system windows and apps, rather than making it dynamic based on the UI elements present in a window’s menu bar.

Although Apple’s intentions were deliberate, many assumed the inconsistent corner radii were a bug, prompting Apple to specifically call attention to the change during the WWDC keynote.

An equally divisive design decision Apple rolls back with macOS 27 Golden Gate is the sheer number of icons shown alongside menu items. With macOS 26 Tahoe, Apple added symbols next to nearly every command across its apps, an attempt to make menus more visually descriptive that instead drew criticism for making them busier and, in some cases, harder to scan.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has (thankfully) reversed course, removing most of those icons and returning menus to a cleaner, less visually cluttered look.

Other visual tidbits in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and more distinct active windows, both of which were also divisive in macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the new Siri app

This is perhaps the most significant new feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple’s revamped Siri, developed in partnership with Google’s Gemini model, gets its own app, in addition to an in-depth, system-wide integration.

The new Siri AI leverages a new per-device indexing system for the user’s data and lives in both Spotlight and the new Siri app.

The Siri app looks and works just as users are mostly used to with other AI assistant apps: a left-hand panel lists the user’s chat history across all compatible platforms, while the main chat panel lets the user type in prompts, attach images and files, or dictate to start a voice-based conversation. The app also supports search and pinned conversations, which is a nice plus depending on the user’s workflow.

The new Siri AI can pull information from the web and the user’s context to provide useful, actionable answers. During the beta period, the new Siri received overwhelmingly positive feedback, even though it can sometimes be slower than users accustomed to other LLM-powered AI assistants expect.

Another useful ability of the new Siri AI is its ability to interact with native and third-party apps, in addition to taking actions directly, taking the app integration available with the old Siri significantly further.

Importantly, developers need to expose their apps’ content and capabilities through the App Intents framework, so expect this aspect of the new assistant to improve over time as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Finally, there is a systemwide “Ask Siri” option in context menus that lets users select text, images, or files and ask Siri about them directly. For example, users can Control-click an image in a document and ask Siri to help them learn more about it, or select a portion of text and ask Siri to rewrite it, proofread it, change its tone, or provide feedback on the writing.

Siri AI is available in English at launch, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish coming in October. For now, Siri AI won’t be available in China or in the EU due to regulatory issues.

Apple Intelligence

We went in-depth on Apple’s new foundation models here, but the gist is that for its 2027 OS releases, the company developed a new version of its Apple Intelligence models. Here’s Apple on each one:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion-parameter dense model that delivers a step up in quality.

AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model. It’s natively multimodal, enabling helpful features like expressive voices and higher-accuracy dictation. Built on cutting-edge Apple research, this 20-billion-parameter model uses a sparse architecture, activating just 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time depending on the request. AFM 3 Core Advanced is unlocked by and optimized for our most capable Apple silicon systems.

AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse, optimized for speed, efficiency, and performance.

ADM 3 Cloud (Image), for image generation and editing, which unlocks advanced photo-editing tools, the all-new Image Playground, and more.

AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most capable server-based model, which powers our most demanding use cases, like agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate leverages two local models, AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced, while the other models are cloud-based. The performance of these two local models depends on the Mac’s hardware, particularly how much memory it has available to run their active parameters and other AI workloads.

When it comes to how Apple Intelligence is implemented in macOS 27 Golden Gate, it is somewhat of a mixed bag. The models themselves are quite good for everyday tasks, such as getting help to draft an e-mail, proofreading a document, or summarizing text.

The problem is that Apple is currently going somewhat overboard on how and when Siri AI is presented to the user, which can sometimes be a bit overwhelming or get in the way of what the user is trying to accomplish.

One great Apple Intelligence addition to macOS 27 Golden Gate is a new Visual Intelligence shortcut. By pressing Command-Shift-Space, users can select any region of the display and immediately ask Siri about it. That works with images, PDFs, text, or just about anything else shown on screen.

Alas, not every macOS 27-compatible Mac will run the new Apple Intelligence, which requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here’s Apple’s official list of Macs that support the new features:

MacBook Neo (2026)

MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

MacBook Pro with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)

Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

Mac Studio (2022 and later)

Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features are available in the same languages supported by the current version of Apple Intelligence, including Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Apple Intelligence is currently unavailable in China due to regulatory issues. Additionally, Apple says there will be usage limits for certain Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features, although the company has yet to share specific details on that.

Performance and reliability improvements

During the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted dozens upon dozens of improvements coming to all its operating systems.

On macOS 27 Golden Gate, this means faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (particularly for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with selective priority syncing.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves Safari and Calendar scrolling, as well as the animations in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple also tweaked Mail indexing and search, as well as the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other tidbits include improved window position consistency and persistence across external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, a broader range of high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes for external monitors, and more complete touch support in Sidecar, including tapping controls, one-finger scrolling, system gestures, and Markup.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces Notify Me, a new Safari feature that can monitor webpages and alert users to relevant changes, such as price drops, product restocks, event registrations opening, or virtually anything else they ask it to track.

Notify Me can check for changes hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, with additional options to specify the days of the week and times when those checks should run.

Additionally, Safari on macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces “Describe an Extension,” which lets users create extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples across productivity, focus, creativity, and design and development. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest.

Both features can be accessed from the “More Options” hamburger menu on the right side of the active Safari tab.

For users who tend to open way too many tabs as the day progresses, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs together based on topic.

Another interesting tidbit in Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new pull-to-refresh gesture, which, like on iOS and iPadOS, lets users refresh the page by swiping down past the rubber-band effect.

This gesture is also available in other system apps, such as Mail, News, and Calendar, which many see as further foreshadowing of touchscreen Macs rumored to be announced as early as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios, a change many saw as an early sign that Apple was preparing the feature for a foldable iPhone.

Well! You can now resize iPhone Mirroring to ANY size! (on an iOS 27-compiled app)

Foldable iPhone is so coming LOL

it doesn't switch to iPad layout though, which is weird… now I am scared for foldable iPhone pic.twitter.com/B9hjxuXWH5

— Dylan (@DylanMcD8) June 8, 2026

Now that the iPhone Duo is official, Mac users can get an early taste of what that experience will look like. Alas, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring remains unavailable in the European Union.

Shortcuts

This is perhaps one of the most useful additions to Apple Intelligence in Apple’s OS updates this year.

Despite its relatively approachable take on automation, Shortcuts can still feel intimidating to more casual users. Now, users can simply describe what they want to accomplish, and Apple Intelligence will build it as a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app also highlights several suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

Dictate and translate to Spanish

Write a weather forecast haiku

Play my exercise playlist when I arrive at the gym

Create a recipe from these leftovers

Summarize my day every morning

Prioritize my to-do list every morning

When I get in the car, get directions

Dictate my idea and save it to the clipboard

Dim screen brightness when Bedtime begins

Turn on Do Not Disturb when I open the TV app

As a side note, if you’d like to get deeper into Shortcuts, make sure to follow Stephen Robles’s fantastic work on YouTube and on Instagram. Also, check out Shortcuts Playground, from MacStories, an even more powerful natural-language-based shortcut creation tool.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three Apple Intelligence-powered editing tools: an enhanced version of Clean Up, which removes objects, people, or other undesired elements from photos; Extend, which generates the surrounding area of an image in case the user decides the original photo is too cropped-in; and Spatial Reframing, which lets users change the angle and composition of a photo after it has been taken.

Additionally, iCloud Shared Albums now supports full-resolution sharing and lets Windows and Android users join in via iCloud.com.

Other new features include playing any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transition styles, and duration, photo ratings with a new star system, and a new, dedicated “Captured by Me” collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate tidbits

Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.

Finder can now intelligently suggest file and folder names, based on their contents.

Image Playgrounds expands support for different styles, and leverages a new foundation model for even better results

Maps gets an enhanced Flyover experience with improved textures, more details, and sharper rendering for hundreds of cities around the world.

Messages now (finally) consolidates tapback notifications and improves syncing across devices.

*Notes supports trackpad-handwritten notes and sketches, expands Markdown support with copy/paste, and adds Section Links.

Podcasts now supports video podcasts, complete with support for picture and picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the final release to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, “only apps will no longer run on Mac computers with Apple silicon after this update,” and you can read more about that here.

Compatibility

According to Apple’s official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Macs:

MacBook Neo (2026)

MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

MacBook Pro with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)

Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

Mac Studio (2022 and later)

Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)

Do you have a favorite new feature? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google rolling out Android 17 QPR1 for Pixel
snippet: Following an extended beta period, Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Google Pixel devices with the September 2026 Feature Drop and security patch. more…
fullText:
Following an extended beta period, Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Google Pixel devices with the September 2026 Feature Drop and security patch.

There are a number of interface changes in Android 17 QPR1, starting with more blur effects across the system UI. The volume panel is where you’ll most likely notice the Dynamic Color-themed translucency, with the full bottom sheet also updated. The Power menu has also been refreshed and is joined by a background blur. This matches the updates that the widgets picker received in the initial Android 17 June release.

The system media player has a new Material 3 carousel-based interface when there are multiple apps. Instead of dots at the bottom, you now see a preview of other open applications, with your current card shrinking to make room.

When opening Quick Settings, you’ll notice a new bouncy animation, while there’s a new icon in the bottom-right corner for making edits.

	

The Mobile Data Tile has been updated with a “Don’t ask me again” toggle. There’s also a new QS Tile for “Keyboard” that lets you access the system switcher. The Screen recording tool now defaults to the last-used application.

When long-pressing on homescreen apps, the menu has been split into app Shortcuts and system Actions (like Bubble and Widgets).

Meanwhile, holding down on an empty homescreen spot reveals an updated fast wallpaper switcher that has more pronounced corner rounding, while the gaps between menu items have been removed. Other changes include:

There’s a new M3 Expressive Settings app icon that was first introduced on the Pixel Watch.

New animation when launching the camera from lockscreen with power button double-tap.

Health Connect on phones can now track distance and calories burned in addition to step count.

Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out starting today for the Pixel 6, Pixel 6 Pro, Pixel 6a, Pixel 7, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7a, Pixel Tablet, Pixel Fold, Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 8a, Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 10a, Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

Visit Settings > System > System update and click the “Check for update” button if the OTA hasn’t already appeared on your device. Android 17 QPR1 Beta 9 users will get a small update to this final release.

The Android Beta Program will remain open and continue testing QPRs and feature drops. 

To get the stable version, those running the Android 17 QPR1 Beta have to opt out first. Devices will not be wiped by the stable OTA once that becomes widely available.

title: Amazon says Fire TV devices will be able to sideload Android apps again in upcoming update
snippet: Fire TV hardware will be able to sideload apps again with an upcoming Android software update for Amazon’s streaming hardware after a previous patch blocked third-party apps. more…
fullText:
Fire TV hardware will be able to sideload apps again with an upcoming Android software update for Amazon’s streaming hardware after a previous patch blocked third-party apps.

Late last year, Amazon rolled out a series of software patches to its Fire TV hardware. On the surface, the Android update for the streaming devices contained the usual security patches and performance updates. It was later discovered that the update disabled sideloading on certain Fire TV devices, preventing third-party apps from being installed if they didn’t come from certified app stores.

Amazon recently commented on that aspect of its previous Android updates in a response to AFTV News. Amazon says sideload prevention is part of a bug in the update, and it wasn’t an intentional aspect of the patch.

If users attempted to install a third-party app, the Fire TV device would list an error and block the process. It didn’t appear to affect all Fire TV devices, though the issue was widespread enough to be considered intentional. According to Amazon, it wasn’t.

	

There was a bug in a recent Fire TV Settings update that caused the “Install unknown apps” list to appear incomplete or empty on some Fire TV devices. We have identified the cause and a fix will roll out in an upcoming Fire TV Settings update, installed automatically on affected devices over the coming week.

This comes as the company recently announced its latest Fire TV Stick, which runs on Vega OS – not Android. It also confirmed that all future Fire TV Stick devices would run Linux-based software in lieu of Google’s OS to achieve a better performance-to-power ratio.

In essence, existing Fire TV devices will seemingly be able to sideload apps again, but that likely won’t be the case for streaming hardware Amazon launches in the future. Amazon says the patch will roll out to affected devices “over the coming week.”

title: YouTube’s login-breaking bug is getting a fix on TVs and consoles
snippet: Users met with an error at login, preventing them from accessing their YouTube account on TVs, and some consoles will be happy to know Google is rolling out a fix. more…
fullText:
Users met with an error at login, preventing them from accessing their YouTube account on TVs, and some consoles will be happy to know Google is rolling out a fix.

An issue began popping up for some users in the last couple of days, preventing a successful login on the TV or console app. Even with the proper password, some users were reporting they were unable to log back in after being kicked out. The issue seemed to persist on Xbox, PlayStation consoles, smart TVs, and streaming hardware – what YouTube classifies as “licing room devices.”

According to YouTube, the login bug that logged users out and blocked them from re-entry has been fixed. YouTube says the issue has been investigated and is now “fully fixed” in a community post separate from existing threads.

It’s unclear when this issue truly began, but there have been several new threads posted on Reddit within the last 24 hours, suggesting the bug affected a wide number of users worldwide.

	

The community post didn’t suggest an app update was needed. It was likely a server-side bug blocking Google Accounts from access, and in some cases, guest accounts.

Did YouTube block you from logging in? Is it fixed for you now?

⭐️ Starred

We’ve known for years that Apple was building a foldable phone, which means that Samsung, the company that popularized the format, also knew. So in July, when the company unveiled the Galaxy Z Fold 8, a wide foldable with proportions similar to the rumored iPhone Duo, it was seen largely as a preemptive move to claim, once again, that Samsung was ahead of the curve.

	

And thankfully the phone was a success; it sold better than expected, and Samsung has been left scrambling for components from next year’s model to satisfy demand today.

But Samsung, as it is wont to do, couldn’t let the phone’s success just speak. It had to inject itself into the conversation around the iPhone Duo in a series of posts that can only be described as cringe. To me, it’s another case of this “I don’t think about you at all” meme.

Of course, this is just silly stuff, but it speaks to the perception that even when Samsung leads, it follows. The good news is that, as Samsung points out in this funny but awkward ad called “Switchers,” it’s now much easier to move from iPhone to Android since Apple and Google collaborated on a new framework.

Samsung appears to be taking the Duo’s release in stride, doubling down on its commitment to foldables by reportedly moving up the release of its second-generation TriFold.

Apple on wide Android foldables beating iPhone Duo; ‘They got the aspect ratio’

✉️ Inbox

Android rolling out passkey transfers between password managers. It’s no longer difficult to transfer credentials between password managers, but passkeys have always been another matter. This system-level change is more than welcome.

Samsung’s first Android XR glasses with a color display may launch in late 2027. We’re only a month or so away from Samsung’s first smart glasses released in collaboration with Google, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster, so it’s no surprise that by the end of next year there will be an option with a display.

Google brings Gemini for desktop app to Windows. It feels like it’s been forever since Google announced a Windows version of its popular Gemini app, but it’s now available and appears fully featured.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 needs battery banks that actually fit; iPhone Duo might help. One benefit of Apple launching a similarly sized foldable is that accessory makers may unintentionally make things better on the Android side.

Possible Google device at FCC could be Wear OS-powered fitness tracker. It would not surprise me if Google is working on more fitness trackers after the runaway success of the Fitbit Air. Hope this one lacks a screen, too.

Welcome to a new project I’m calling Cc:, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. This week, I’m speaking with my friend and former colleague, Nicholas Sutrich.

Who are you?

Nicholas Sutrich

What do you do for work?

I’m the Senior Content Producer at Android Central. This is a fancy title that really means I test a lot of devices every week and write about them.

What do you do for fun?

I reviewed devices for 10 years on the side before going full-time, so I still like to think of my job as being a fun hobby I just so happen to get paid for. Other than work, I love video gaming with my wife and son, reading novels, gardening and chicken tending, CrossFit, and the occasional hike when I can squeeze it in.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

I spend less time on my phone now than maybe ever. I’ve deleted all social media off my phone (otherwise, I find I work too much for my own good), and I don’t generally play games on my phone unless I’m doing it for a review. My goal is to get off my devices when work is over and spend more quality time with friends and family in person, instead. 

What are a few apps you can’t live without and why?

eMeals: A meal planning service I subscribe to. It’s $5 a month and has a boatload of recipes on there, plus new recipes each week and plans for specific dietary restrictions, stores, or budgets.

Zepp: This is the app for Amazfit smartwatches. I use it for food logging and for workout logging. The food logging portion is particularly fantastic because it’s LLM-driven, so you can tell it you had “2 eggs fried in coconut oil with 2 slices of avocado toast and a glass of orange juice for breakfast” and it’ll log all that crap instantly. No more scrolling through tedious lists.

Discord: Everyone probably uses this, but it’s my main chat app with friends. We bounced between apps for years until it came out and haven’t switched since. 

What is a gadget that you love right now?

Motorola Razr Fold. This phone is just such a joy to use. Excellent camera and displays, never have to worry about battery life. Software is snappy and has great features (double-chop for flashlight, woot!). Oh, and the sides are CURVED, not friggin’ flat. I hate stupid phones with flat sides, especially foldables.

What’s a recent TV show you loved?

Gotta be Pursuit of Jade on Netflix. It’s a time period drama/romance/kung-fu show set in ancient China. We randomly tried it after The Algorithm™️ recommended it to us and haven’t stopped since. We only watch like 20-30 mins of TV a day tops, so it’s taken a while to get through all 40 episodes, especially since they’re usually 45 minutes or so apiece.

What’s a recent book you loved?

Jurassic Park by Michael Crichton. I somehow never read these books (although I love the OG movie). It was fun reading the original content and seeing the author’s direction for the story versus the films. Also fascinating to see what parts of the book the films stripped out and randomly slapped into other movies.

What’s a recent movie you loved?

Project Hail Mary. I read this book twice (one of which was out loud to my family) and was so happy that they were making a movie. It’s such an excellent mix of science reality and science fiction in a unique end-of-times scenario. If aliens exist, I hope they’re like Rocky.

What’s a recent game you loved?

Orbitals for the Nintendo Switch 2. I’ve played many co-op games in my time, but few are as well produced and executed as Orbitals. The visuals are beyond stunning and make you feel like you’re playing a Studio Ghibli movie. It’s basically impossible to describe the gameplay other than a wild mix of adventure, puzzle, and platforming.

What’s something offline you do every day that brings you joy?

Family reading time. We’ve done this since our son was little and it never ceases to be wonderful. At the end of most days (I wish we did it every day), we’ll curl up in bed or on the couch and read together. Sometimes, it’s reading manga; other times, it’s an audiobook or reading aloud to each other. We’ve gone through a lot of books this way, and it’s a great way to spend quality time together, drink some tea, have snacks, and start conversations.

Thank you, Nick, for being awesome as always. See you on the putting green.

Over the weekend, American AI titans, including Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman, xAI’s Elon Musk, and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis, came out in support of “pacing the frontier,” a term popularized by a letter released in July by nearly 1,400 employees of large American AI companies.

In fact, Amodei wrote his own 3,000+ word paean called “We Must Pace the Frontier,” in which he posits that the industry needs to slow down its frenetic work on improving AI model capabilities in order to prioritize alignment and safety.

“Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails.”

This self-policed slowdown comes as the US government continues to distance itself from regulation, despite entreaties from both sides of the aisle, as well as countries around the world. In a Truth Social post, President Trump said that “the only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so.”

In more than 100 countries, Apple has launched a new initiative that bundles Apple TV and Apple Arcade subscriptions into iCloud+, at no extra charge. title: Here’s what’s new with parental control features in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27
snippet: Included in today’s 2027 system updates from Apple are several new Screen Time and parental control features aimed at giving parents more control over how their kids use their devices. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Included in today’s 2027 system updates from Apple are several new Screen Time and parental control features aimed at giving parents more control over how their kids use their devices. Here are the details.

Today’s updates include important parental control improvements

Apple today released iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 with what it describes as a “new suite of powerful, intuitive, and easy-to-use tools that helps parents create safer digital experiences for their kids,” many of which the company previewed in June, during the WWDC26 keynote.

In essence, the new features focus on four areas: what content kids can access, who they can communicate with, when they can use their devices, and how parents can manage those controls.

All of them fall under the protections and restrictions of Child Accounts, which Apple says are required for children under 13, or the equivalent minimum age in their country or region, and available for children up to 18.

With iOS 27, Apple has also simplified the setup process for new Child Accounts. Parents can start with a small set of essential apps, a recommended starter set, or choose exactly which Apple apps their child can access from the outset.

Once a parent sets up a Child Account, they can choose which apps and websites their child can access, as well as set age and content restrictions for movies, TV shows, music, books, and other media.

Parents can now also rely on Ask to Browse, a feature that lets kids request access to blocked websites in Safari across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with parents approving requests in Messages. This is similar to Ask to Buy, which already requires parental approval before children can download apps or make in-app purchases.

Parents can also require kids to ask for approval before connecting with new contacts, set shared or individual daily limits for categories such as Entertainment, Games, and Social Media, and create schedules that determine which apps are available at different times of day. Those schedules can also vary depending on the day of the week.

Screen Time itself has also been redesigned, with a new architecture that Apple says makes parental controls sync more quickly across devices in a Family Sharing group. Parents can now see weekly usage summaries and their kids’ most-used apps at a glance, temporarily pause access to a device, open things back up for a limited period, and quickly switch between different schedules.

Communication Safety is also expanding beyond nudity detection. The feature can now block detected gore or violent content in shared images and videos, while displaying a warning and additional resources.

Time Allowances are also more flexible. Parents can create their own app categories, move apps between them, and assign a time allowance as soon as they approve a new app through Ask to Buy. Websites associated with an app can also automatically follow the same allowance.

Apple says its suggested Time Allowances are based on a child’s age and expert research. The company is also working with the American Academy of Pediatrics to adapt its Family Media Plan into guidance for parents using Apple products.

Finally, Apple notes that all devices in a Family Sharing group need to be running the version 27 software releases to use the new Screen Time experience.

title: MagSafe Monday: Vinich’s MagSafe wallet leans into a classic look
snippet: I’ve been on a spree of trying out new MagSafe wallets that look more like traditional wallets. Vinich’s MagSafe wallet is the latest one I’ve tried. It comes in 15+ colors, looks like a traditional foldable wallet built to sit on the back of a leather iPhone case without clashing with it. It’s designed to look more like an extension of your iPhone case. more…
fullText:
I’ve been on a spree of trying out new MagSafe wallets that look more like traditional wallets. Vinich’s MagSafe wallet is the latest one I’ve tried. It comes in 15+ colors, looks like a traditional foldable wallet built to sit on the back of a leather iPhone case without clashing with it. It’s designed to look more like an extension of your iPhone case.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Color options

The manufacturer clearly wanted to leave no stone unturned when it came to colors. They have options in black, green, brown, and even purple, all with a broken-in, aged look that goes well with a leather case rather than fighting it. They also have countless other colors as well. Vinich also offers Desert Titanium, which goes well with that color iPhone if you opt for a caseless look.

Wallet sotrage

Vinich lists three card slots and says you can realistically fit three to five cards, depending on their thickness. In day-to-day usage, that’s probably a driver’s license, a card or two, and a work access control card. There’s also room to fold a bill or two behind the cards, which I always appreciate in a wallet this size. I try to always keep $20 or so on me

The card compartment is lined with RFID-blocking material, and the interior is lined with microfiber so your cards aren’t rubbing against fabric all day. The magnets are strong enough here. I’ve had stronger ones, but I’ve also had much weaker ones.

Three things to know before you buy

First, this is synthetic leather, not actual real leather. It’s scratch-resistant with reinforced stitching, and at this price point, that’s exactly what you’d expect, but if you’re pairing it with a real leather case, you should know going in that the materials aren’t going to be an exact match. Vinich recommends conditioning it every three to six months

Second, it can slowly inch into the frame on wide-angle and macro shots. It sits below the camera on most iPhones, but for close-up photography, you’ll want to pull it off to make sure it’s not covering the lens at all

Finally, it does not work as a stand, even though it looks like it should. The flap is intentionally flexible to keep stress off the magnetic ring, so if you want a wallet that props your iPhone up for a call or video, this isn’t it.

Wrap up

Sub $25, the color range alone makes this worth a look if you’ve been running a nice leather case with a wallet that doesn’t match it. Most MagSafe wallets are built to disappear. This one is built to go with something, and it feels/looks more like a traditional wallet you’d even carry standalone as well. I’d love to see an option with Find Me integration in the future as well. 

You can buy the Vinich MagSafe wallet from Amazon or directly from Vinich.

title: iOS 26.7 now available for iPhone, here’s what’s new
snippet: Apple launched its major iOS 27 release today for iPhone. But for anyone not yet ready to install the new software version, Apple has also released a smaller iOS 26.7 update. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Apple launched its major iOS 27 release today for iPhone. But for anyone not yet ready to install the new software version, Apple has also released a smaller iOS 26.7 update. Here’s what’s new.

iOS 26.7 debuts as security fix update for iPhone users not yet ready to install iOS 27

It’s a big day for Apple software releases. The company just debuted iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, watchOS 27, and a lot more.

But if you’re not ready to install the latest software yet, Apple has another option for you.

iOS 26.7 is now available for iPhone, a minor update for anyone not yet ready to install iOS 27.

The new release includes “security fixes for your iPhone” per Apple’s official release notes.

It’s become common practice for Apple to ship smaller updates to its current OS version on the same day as major new releases debut.

The company typically presents iPhone users with two options. They can install the major new release, or stay on the current version and get additional security updates and bug fixes.

Today, iOS 26.7 is that second option. It doesn’t contain any new features, but it does ensure your iPhone stays up to date with the latest security patches.

The full list of security fixes has been published here. It’s an extensive list of patches, highlighting the importance of installing the update despite its lack of other improvements.

Are you upgrading to iOS 27 or keeping your iPhone on iOS 26.7 for now? Let us know in the comments.

title: Samsung reportedly considers early ‘Galaxy Z TriFold 2’ release in wake of iPhone Duo
snippet: In the wake of iPhone Duo, Samsung is reportedly considering an early release for a Galaxy Z TriFold sequel. more…
fullText:
In the wake of iPhone Duo, Samsung is reportedly considering an early release for a Galaxy Z TriFold sequel.

The Galaxy Z TriFold delivered a wild new form factor to Samsung’s lineup late last year, but it didn’t stick around for long. The TriFold made its US debut in January for $2,900 and was discontinued barely three months later.

There have been rumors flying around a “Galaxy Z TriFold 2” coming in 2027 alongside another new form factor, a slideable, but it sounds like that might be moved up following Apple’s iPhone Duo reveal. 

Leaker Lanzuk says that Samsung is “considering” an early “Galaxy Z TriFold 2” release, with the slideable also being moved up. An exact timeline is unclear, and it’s likely enough that the 2027 timeline will remain.

	

The post also claims that the TriFold sequel will be “thinner, lighter, and more durable” compared to the first generation, with a goal of having the price be “nearly identical.” While $2,899 is still no small price to pay, it’d be impressive if Samsung were able to keep pricing unchanged given the market forces at play, not to mention rumors that the first TriFold was sold at a loss. 

Would you buy a second-generation TriFold?

title: Googlebook pre-orders start on September 21
snippet: After previously teasing a fall timeframe, Google is set to open pre-orders for Googlebooks on Monday, September 21. more…
fullText:
After previously teasing a fall timeframe, Google is set to open pre-orders for Googlebooks on Monday, September 21.

The email blast to users who signed up for updates on the Android-based platform went out this morning. On September 21 at 9 a.m. ET, you’ll be able to pre-order the first Googlebook devices.

You can expect devices from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, with several leaking in recent weeks. By that date, Google will presumably detail the full operating system, including sharing what the actual name is. In May, we only got a preview.

Today’s teaser highlights the Magic Pointer that allows you to access Gemini immediately. This animation transforms into the light bar that all Googlebooks are expected to feature as their marquee branding element. Google has yet to share what exactly it will do. Compared to Chromebooks, this will be the primary brand on the cover. “Googlebooks” only appears on the left palm rest just below the keyboard. 

	

It’s not clear what the gap between pre-orders and device shipments will be, but launching before the holiday shopping season seems likely.

title: YouTube details NFL Sunday Ticket pricing & availability for 2026 season, including a 50% discount
snippet: YouTube is starting its fourth season as the home of NFL Sunday Ticket and, ahead of Week 1 games, an overview of availability and pricing has been detailed, including a big discount for new customers. more…
fullText:
YouTube is starting its fourth season as the home of NFL Sunday Ticket and, ahead of Week 1 games, an overview of availability and pricing has been detailed, including a big discount for new customers.

For the 2026-2027 season, NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV will start at $240/year.

That’s thanks to a big discount YouTube is running, but it’s only available for new subscribers. For those eligible, it’s a discount of up to 50%. For existing customers, the costs are $378/year through YouTube TV (in addition to monthly subscription costs) or $480/year through YouTube Primetime Channels.

You can sign up via YouTube’s Sunday Ticket website.

	

NFL Sunday Ticket packages at YouTube

On a support page and through a thread on Reddit, Google details what games are and are not available through NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube this year, and where you can watch those other games.

It breaks down to:

Thursday Night Football: Not available on YouTube/YouTube TV

Sunday Afternoon Games: Out-of-market via Sunday Ticket, in-market via CBS or Fox on YouTube TV, in-market via Paramount+ or Fox One on YouTube

Sunday Night Football: NBC via YouTube TV, Peacock via YouTube

Monday Night Football: ABC/ESPN via YouTube TV, not available on YouTube

NFL Sunday Ticket also does not include preseason or postseason games, as well as some regular season games such as Thanksgiving Day games.

For Week 1 games being played on September 13, YouTube details what games will be broadcast via CBS and Fox and, as such, are not on Sunday Ticket if you live within the local region. So, as an example: If you live in Buffalo, NY, CBS will be broadcasting the Bills at Texans game, which will not be available via Sunday Ticket, but that game will be on Sunday Ticket if you live in Washington, DC.
